newsitem.title: USA: Bergen, IVAX to merge in stock deal.
newsitem.headline: Bergen, IVAX to merge in stock deal.

text.p: Drug wholesaler Bergen Brunswig Corp. and generic drug maker IVAX Corp. said Monday they were merging in a tax-free stock deal, but the shares of both fell sharply on the news.
The two companies said in a statement they were forming a new company, BBI Healthcare Corp., which will acquire California-based Bergen Brunsnwig and Florida-based IVAX through an exchange of stock.
However, IVAX's stock lost about 18 percent and Bergen Brunswig slipped 13 percent as investors reactly cooly to the announcement.
Based on trading prices at midday Monday, the transaction would be worth about $2.70 billion.
IVAX fell $2.875 to $12.875 on the American Stock Exchange while Bergen Brunswig dropped $4 to $28.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Miami-based IVAX said separately that it posted a net loss of $178.7 million, or $1.47 a share, in the third quarter after suffering a 28 percent drop in revenues and taking $128 million in pre-tax charges.
The proposed merger would create the nation's only fully integrated manufacturer and distributor of products to the pharmaceutical and acute care markets, the companies said.
IVAX holders will own about 56 percent of the new company's 91 million shares, while Bergen holders will own about 44 percent.
The announcement said IVAX holders will receive 0.42 share of stock in the new company for each IVAX share, and Bergen Brunswig holders will receive one share of BBI for each share of Bergen.
Shares in BBI are expected to be traded on the New York Stock Exchange after the deal closes early next year.

The announcement said the new company was being formed at a time when some $48 billion in annual sales of branded pharmaceuticals will become available in the next five years for generic substitution.
Bergen Brunswig Chairman Robert Martini and IVAX Chairman Phillip Frost will serve as co-chairmen of the new company, which will be based in Miami and have about 12,000 employees.
Bergen Brunswig President Donald R. Roden will become chief executive of BBI.

"This combination will enhance revenues, take advantage of synergies by streamlining the supply chain, improve margins, and create shareholder value that exceeds the value of Bergen and IVAX as stand-alone businesses," Martini said in a statement.

The merger also expands Bergen's business outside the United States for the first time. IVAX's Norton Healthcare subsidiary is the largest generic pharmaceutical company in Britain and serves as the hub of operations in Ireland, Poland, Germany, the Czech and Slovak Republics, and China.

"We are combining our efficient organisation and consistent financial performance with IVAX's innovation and higher margins," Martini said. "Together, we will deliver earnings growth and the broadest, most technically advanced generic drug product line in the world."
BBI Healthcare's board will have seven members designated by IVAX and seven members designated by Bergen Brunswig, which is based in Orange, Calif.

IVAX, which has been hurt by strong competition in the generic drug industry, said its revenues for the third quarter fell to $222.7 million from to $310.2 million, primarily due to lower prices, higher customer inventories and reduced promotional activities.
The company also said its net loss for the first nine months almost doubled to $158.8 million, or $1.31 a share, from $79.0 million, or 67 cents a share.
Revenues for the period fell to $830.6 million from $898.0 million.
The company also said it omitted its semi-annual dividend for the second half of 1996. In June it paid a semi-annual dividend of 5 cents a share to holders of record on May 10.
On Sunday Bergen Brunswig declared a regular quarterly dividend of 12 cents a share cash payable Dec. 2 for holders on Nov. 18.
The two companies said they expect the new company to pay annual dividends of 48 cents a share.
